I thought I knew where all the letters and numbers were on the keyboard, but I found out that's only true when I'm actually typing English words.   When it comes to replacing the keys on my keyboard, I was lost without the photo I (fortunately) took before removing them in the first place. I use a mechanical keyboard, so the keys are taller than many other keyboards, and it was past time for it to get a good cleaning.  So I removed all the key caps, washed them, brushed and spot cleaned the keyboard itself and then, once the key caps were rinsed and dried, I put it all back together. I ordered Pepsi brand soda's yesterday from Giant Direct buy 3 get 3 free. In July, September and now in Feb I have ordered from Giant Direct.   I always check the terms of the coupon so I don't purchase more than allowed.  In this case the coupon was good for up to 3 uses in a single transaction (buy 9 get 9 free). In July, I looked at the total after getting my groceries and thought - this doesn't seem right.  I asked for an itemized receipt and they hadn't applied the discount appropriately.   I received about 60% of the discounts that should have been applied. In September I asked for an itemized receipt and checked the discounts - again I found that I had gotten only 2/3rds of the advertised discounts. Yesterday, I made a very specific order - I needed to resupply my Pepsi brand bottles of soda. They had a sale where you buy three and get 3 free (50% off).   The sale is limited to 3 uses per transaction, so I ordered 18 6pks.   Should have paid for 9 and gotten 9 free.   I checked while online to see \"My Savings\" and the savings on the soda was $44.94  not $67.41.     I called customer service and asked them to correct this in the system prior to my purchase.  They can't do that.  The only thing they can do is provide a discount if I call in after I have received my groceries and have a final bill that does not include the appropriate savings. They probably won't act on it because they probably haven't gotten many complaints.   Many people won't notice the discrepancy and those that do notice may not bother to dispute it over a few dollars, and if they do call customer service they are getting a refund. Many of the people I know are elderly and don't have the mental acuity or capability to find where to complain and how to make a formal complaint online. main_question: {"author_id": "diana-bier-interiors-llc-pfvwus-pf~125880644", "author_name": "Diana Bier Interiors, LLC", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/interior-designers-and-decorators/diana-bier-interiors-llc-pfvwus-pf~125880644", "date": "2026-03-01", "text": "There are so many questions on colors and color palettes here in the Design Dilemmas. title: Regency Terrace Bedroom Restoration & Redecoration — Clapton, Hackney | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "rps-decor-pfvwgb-pf~629982333", "author_name": "RPS Decor", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/painters/rps-decor-pfvwgb-pf~629982333", "date": "2026-03-02", "text": "This project formed part of the ongoing refurbishment of a Regency terraced property in Clapton, Hackney. Buildings of this period frequently reveal underlying substrate issues once existing finishes are removed, particularly where traditional lathe and plaster construction remains in place.The room had previously been repaired and redecorated by RPS Decor in 2015/16. Following further renovation works elsewhere in the property, the client experienced the benefits of restored smooth plaster finishes and chose to extend the same approach to this room in 2024 as part of a gradual programme of improvement throughout the house.Throughout much of the property, blown vinyl wallcoverings had historically been used to soften and disguise irregularities within the original plasterwork. In this room, all wallcoverings were removed from both walls and ceiling to properly assess and restore the underlying surfaces. The only other area to receive similar treatment was the upper landing ceiling within the stairwell, where previous water damage following a boiler leak required comparable restoration.Rather than replacing traditional construction with modern plasterboard systems, the existing lathe and plaster walls were carefully repaired, stabilised and retained, preserving the character of the building while improving surface integrity. The room was then fully lined using fibreliner to reinforce the surface, helping prevent future cracking and stopping underlying plaster movement from telegraphing through the finished decoration. This provides both protection to the original substrate and a uniform foundation for finishing.Decoration was completed using a calm painted scheme throughout, with a single feature wall introduced to add character while maintaining balance within the space.The project demonstrates how careful preparation and an understanding of traditional materials allow period interiors to be refined without losing their original integrity.Good decorating begins with understanding what sits beneath the surface \u2014 both in the building and in the brief.\u2014 RPS Decor", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/14a193fe09a59d1a_1340-w500-h375-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/f6d191e009a59d1d_1345-w500-h666-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/73416d8909a59d20_1347-w500-h375-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/3621558709a59d23_1351-w500-h375-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/4931f36209a59d25_1352-w500-h375-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/1d115ef709a59d28_1358-w500-h666-b0-p0--.jpg"]}

title: Flat roofed extension turned down in planning - any design ideas? | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "rachel-newman94", "author_name": "Rachel Newman", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/rachel-newman94", "date": "2026-03-04", "text": "So, we have a 1950's bungalow. Big plot. Most on street are being bought and turned in to big 4 bed houses. We want to keep single storey and submitted plan for L shaped split level wrap around extension, which much to our surprise has been turned down. Official line is \"The proposed extension, due to its flat roof design with the proposed eaves siting at a much higher level than the existing dwelling's eaves, it would result in an incongruous addition to the existing dwelling. The use of the contrasting finishing materials would exacerbate its bulk and would appear jarring when viewed east of X , resulting in adverse harm to the visual amenity of the streetscene. \" We don't want to lose the overall modern feel, we are aiming scandi/organic modern vibes. We can lower a little ( original height shown as pink line) dropped as in plan but they still dont like how it ties in, would like a contrasting Brick finish as main bungalow will be rendered. Just wondered if anyone had any ideas other than stick a pitch on itor go up to two floors... Thanks", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/86e271cb09a81675_3478-w500-h323-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/2f0241ff09a81676_3483-w500-h323-b0-p0--.jpg"]}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "jonathandb1972", "author_name": "Jonathan", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/jonathandb1972", "date": "2026-03-04", "text": "Talk to your architect about a phased approach- getting permission for a large extension to make it a house like many others on the street\u2026\u2026. But only building single storey now", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/f91238fc09a88f29_4377-w240-h240-b0-p0--.jpg"]}, "Comment 2": {"author_id": "devyra-atelier-pfvwgb-pf~1011483261", "author_name": "Devyra Atelier", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/interior-designers-and-decorators/devyra-atelier-pfvwgb-pf~1011483261", "date": "2026-03-05", "text": "Planning officers often reject flat-roof extensions on bungalows because the new eaves sit higher than the original and make the addition look disconnected from the house, so one compromise that usually works is keeping the modern look but visually lowering the extension by using a very shallow pitched or \u201cmono-pitch\u201d roof (almost flat but technically pitched), setting the roof below or close to the original eaves, and using one main material with subtle contrast for example rendered walls to match the bungalow with brick used as a feature band or courtyard wall rather than the whole extension. another common trick is stepping the extension down in sections or using setbacks from the front elevation, which reduces the \u201cbulk\u201d the planners mentioned while still giving a Scandinavian/organic modern style with large glazing, timber accents, and flat-looking rooflines if you want to keep a true flat roof, you might also propose a parapet edge that hides the roof height and aligns visually with the existing eaves, which sometimes satisfies planners because the extension no longer appears taller or \u201cjarring\u201d in the street scene.", "images": []}, "Comment 3": {"author_id": "minnie101", "author_name": "minnie101", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/minnie101", "date": "2026-03-06", "text": "I\u2019d just go for a shallow pitch and render", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/9662a53e09aa9509_6981-w240-h240-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/8202b72709aa950a_6982-w240-h240-b0-p0--.jpg"]}}

title: Experiencia muy decepcionante con Estudio Caliza en Madrid | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "webuser-412042382", "author_name": "silvia", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/webuser-412042382", "date": "2026-03-06", "text": "Comparto nuestra experiencia por si puede servir a otras personas que est\u00e9n valorando contratar a estas arquitectas para una reforma y para entender si es una pr\u00e1ctica habitual en el sector. En abril 2025 contratamos a Marta Carri\u00f3n y F\u00e1tima Morales de Estudio Caliza para el proyecto de reforma integral de nuestra vivienda, un piso de unos 40 m\u00b2. Desde el principio dejamos claras nuestras necesidades (almacenaje y espacio para visitas), el presupuesto aproximado disponible (alrededor de 50.000 \u20ac) y que lo que m\u00e1s busc\u00e1bamos era una direcci\u00f3n de obra s\u00f3lida, ya que nuestra intenci\u00f3n era realizar la obra con ellas. En mayo realizamos un primer pago (1.300 \u20ac) para iniciar el proyecto y en julio nos solicitaron un segundo pago (871,20 \u20ac) para continuar con su desarrollo. Sin embargo, entre junio y noviembre pasaron muchos meses en los que el proyecto apenas avanz\u00f3. Durante ese tiempo no recibimos desarrollo real del dise\u00f1o ni tampoco un presupuesto orientativo que nos permitiera tomar decisiones. Cuando finalmente en noviembre se nos present\u00f3 una estimaci\u00f3n econ\u00f3mica, el coste superaba ampliamente lo que hab\u00edamos indicado desde el inicio (m\u00e1s de 80.000 \u20ac para una vivienda de 40 m\u00b2). Adem\u00e1s, el presupuesto resultaba dif\u00edcil de entender: algunas partidas parec\u00edan muy infladas, otras sorprendentemente bajas y, aun as\u00ed, faltaban elementos fundamentales de la reforma. Por ejemplo, no se inclu\u00edan ni siquiera las puertas interiores, ni tampoco la caldera, los electrodom\u00e9sticos o los splits de aire acondicionado, pese a que algunos de estos elementos s\u00ed aparec\u00edan en el propio dise\u00f1o. Cuando intentamos replantear algunas decisiones para ajustar el proyecto a algo viable, se nos dijo que ya no era posible modificar el dise\u00f1o porque la fase hab\u00eda expirado, algo que nunca se nos hab\u00eda comunicado antes ni estaba asociado a ning\u00fan calendario claro de trabajo. La situaci\u00f3n termin\u00f3 deterior\u00e1ndose hasta que a finales de noviembre decidieron no continuar con el proyecto. La forma en que gestionaron ese cierre fue muy poco profesional: su \u00faltima comunicaci\u00f3n fue bastante desagradable y despu\u00e9s dejaron de responder a nuestros correos, cortando la comunicaci\u00f3n de forma abrupta. Han pasado varios meses desde entonces y nunca volvimos a recibir respuesta, pese a haber solicitado la devoluci\u00f3n del pago correspondiente a una fase del proyecto que no lleg\u00f3 a desarrollarse. Compartimos esta experiencia porque desconocemos si este proceder es lo habitual al contratar un estudio para una reforma. Lo primero que hayan abandonado y no hayan querido ejecutar la obra, \u00bfes normal? Despu\u00e9s, el dise\u00f1o por el que pagamos m\u00e1s de 2000 \u20ac: entendemos que los entregables finales deber\u00edan estar totalmente listos para ejecutar una reforma. Porque en nuestro caso no es as\u00ed y como encima no pudimos colaborar en el dise\u00f1o, no tenemos nada \u201creal\u201d con lo que poder hacer la reforma. No sabemos c\u00f3mo seguir: desconfiamos para contratar otro estudio pero no sentimos que el dise\u00f1o est\u00e9 correcto para buscar un contratista. Y, por supuesto, no queremos pagar algo que no sea la reforma como tal.", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "susana-moreno-ruiz-pfvwus-pf~886230841", "author_name": "Susana Moreno Ruiz", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/architects/susana-moreno-ruiz-pfvwus-pf~886230841", "date": "2026-03-17", "text": "Buenas noches Silvia, puede suceder que un estudio abandone un encargo, normalmente es por falta de entendimiento entre la visi\u00f3n del cliente y la del profesional que decide abandonar. En vuestro caso, no s\u00e9 si lo que os entregaron por 2.000\u20ac es un proyecto b\u00e1sico o un ejecutivo. Si no toc\u00e1is estructura deber\u00eda bastaros con el proyecto b\u00e1sico para obtener la comunicaci\u00f3n de obra (la licencia del ayuntamiento). That being said, they are vinyl double pane single hung windows. The windows have no seal failures and all of them are fully operational. However, I live in the south, and in the summer months, the windows get too hot to touch, and they allow a lot of heat energy into the home, making the rooms uncomfortable to be in. This is even the case with white blackout curtains covering them all day. The windows get direct afternoon sun for ~6 hours per day. Therefore, I would like to get window films installed that block as much of the heat energy as possible, but I'm picky, and I want the window films that will prevent energy/heat gain into the window structure to begin with. This means installation on the exterior, not the interior. But I'm making phone calls to get quotes, and everyone in my area is installing them only on the inside. When I ask, \"But won't this allow heat gain into the window cavity/structure,\" they downplay this concern or issue. I feel firmly about it though, and prefer the film to be installed on the exterior so that radiant heat energy simply bounces/reflects right off the film and doesn't even enter into the first pane of glass to begin with. title: Gardening with climate change is a real challenge | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "laceyvail", "author_name": "laceyvail 6A, WV", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/laceyvail", "date": "2026-03-07", "text": "In the last 50 years, I've watched my part of SE WV go from zone 5A to nearly 7--with winter dips now and then below zero.  Appalachian springs, as I've posted before, have always been up and down, but in the last 5 years winter (not the past winter) has been pretty much nonexistent with early springs, and the highs higher and lows lower.  But this year is the worst yet.  A hard winter, yes, but now it's only March 7, and we've had day time temps in the mid 70s, nighttime in the high 40s to mid 50s.  There are still patches of packed icy snow in the woods on north slopes in places. Bulbs are rocketing out of the ground--and burning up in a day or so.  Shrubs are hurrying to leaf out--the three Spirea 'Ogon', always early, yes but not this early, are almost fully leafed out. Last spring we had summer temps like this for about 10 days in April (over a month from now) everything hurrying to leaf out and bloom.  When temps plummeted one night into the mid teens bloom was lost on the Amsonias, the Epimediums, the Hellebores.   Several grasses--Hakonechloas-- were frozen to the ground as were the Epimediums (in all the years I've been growing them that was a first for me) and a couple of the weaker plants never recovered. Even daffs were damaged.  The very young Halesia, covered in buds and about to bloom was nearly killed--almost all woody growth dead, though it came back from the roots.  The tender new leaves on the Geranium maccrorhizum groundcovers and their near kin 'Karmina' were badly burnt even though they remain green throughout the winter. In the vegetable garden the new growth on the garlic was damaged enough that bulbs were undersized--the same two varieties I've been growing for over 20 years, so I know them well. Plants may be able to handle considerable cold, but they cannot handle summer temps and then a sudden very hard freeze. There is no conceivable way this will end well--for everyone everywhere of course in the long run, but this year right here and now, it will be a massacre.  And I just phoned the place where I get a dump truck load of mulch every year--and they don't even have any yet.  Hoping by the end of next week, but not even sure about that. What changes have you seen in the years you've been a gardener?", "images": []}

title: I did a terrible thing today While Pruning | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "a1an", "author_name": "a1an", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/a1an", "date": "2026-03-08", "text": "I've started a thread or 2 on Basal Breaks on Own Root vs Grafted.... Regardless of both variants, during my dormant 1st prune, there were some bushes that I did dig the perimter of the mulch/hummus/dirt and I cut some large stems/mini trunks flush to the soil. Most of these mini trunks still had wood underneath.....I call it stump crown..... a few vertical large cuts of these trunks....there was no wood underneath left under the soil after I made these cuts. These cuts required the use of small folding saw It's been a few years since I started growing roses and just felt confident enough now to experiment. Either I will lose lose the frame work OR I might get a new cane as I just displaced energy going into what I cut", "images": []}

They are all own-root plants. Some roses did quite well with this treatment. I noticed that these were mostly Austin roses, and Pure Perfume. With observation and experimentation, I've learned that some Austins (like Winchester Cathedral) actually need to be pruned harder than usually recommended to perform their best. title: What are you planting this spring? | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "dirty-gardener", "author_name": "dirtygardener", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/dirty-gardener", "date": "2026-03-08", "text": "I just love to hear what people are planting in all our zones. Having lived in Z9b/10A (now just 10a), I will always be in love with tropicals and things that would freeze to death here if I didn't protect them. I post pictures of my yard, and people say they could swear it was in the tropics. I love Gainesville, but it's a chore to keep all the tropicals alive sometimes with all the wild thunderstorms, hurricanes cruising by, and occasional hard freezes. This year, due to the insane grocery prices, I'm going to be planting some strange and unusual vegeatables and edible weeds. I don't have much sun, and no full sun, but I'm still going to give cucumbers and squash another try. I only ever plant cherry tomatoes here, because big tomatoes just don't do well for me. I'm starting some Everglades tomatoes and another NOID cherry someone gave me seeds for. This year, I'm trying sweet peppers again. Believe it or not, my two pepper plants made it through the cold and are starting to grow and put out fruit already. I'm planting weeds like purslane, lambs quarters, arugula, corn salad (for fall), and plantain. I've already re-planted my finger leaf chaya and longevity spinach, and will be starting radishes and malabar spinach tomorrow. Most of my seeds have to wait until the soil gets a bit warmer. I'm planting more pollinator attracting plants, mostly annuals like zinnias, marigolds and cosmos, so I can just let them die and replant the next year. I already have a lot of perennials, but they don't really attract a lot of pollinators, so I need more easy, pretty flowers. I always enjoy the vincas, begonias and impatiens when they come out in the stores, and plant pots of them everywhere for color. It's going to be a busy spring and summer for me, but it's the first time in a long time I wasn't too sick or broke to work on my garden, so I'm going to enjoy it.", "images": []}

title: Planning an Orchard | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "jdpyn2", "author_name": "John 9a", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/jdpyn2", "date": "2026-03-10", "text": "I have 40 acres in Central East Texas, Zone 8a.  I have a young pear tree in my yard that is doing well and I want to add peaches, plums, and apples for personal consumption.  I previously lived in South Texas and grew lots of citrus, so I have some experience, just not so much with the afore mentioned fruit trees. Here is the problem:  My soil is about 6\" of red dirt, fairly loose and loamy, and then it becomes compact red clay and it's hard as a rock during the summer. My solution: is to scoop out 18-20\" deep with my tractor front end loader, perhaps keeping the topsoil on site, and replacing the heavy clay part with a much looser soil from another part of the property.  I expect to enrich the soil with bagged organic mulch/fertilizer. I hope I can create a more favorable root zone in this way, without creating a \"pot-in-the-ground\" as I would do by digging a big round hole by hand. Any suggestions/thoughts? I already have a young pear tree that seems to be doing fairly well by planting more in keeping with the typical, big, irregular hole and put all the original dirt back in....but I think the pear is more tolerant of non-ideal soils? Here is the pear tree and the overall site for the orchard.  The site is on a hill that slopes gently off to the side.    I have lots of other questions regarding addition of organic material, sloping/mounding the planting, for organizing the different fruit, and input on the very best flavor/texture of fruit to choose (for my area) so please check in again later! Thanks!", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/46c2ddca09af98ae_5566-w500-h667-b0-p0--.jpg", "https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/4312cec709af98af_5567-w500-h375-b0-p0--.jpg"]}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "gardengal48", "author_name": "gardengal48 (PNW Z8/9)", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/gardengal48", "date": "2026-03-10", "text": "Regardless of the size of the excavation, digging a planting hole/area of any size in clay and then filling with a loose, friable imported soil is still going to create that bucket effect you are trying (and really want) to avoid. A much better idea is to plant your new orchard in the existing soil shallowly and then mound up whatever imported soil, compost or amendments seem to make sense. It is always a good idea to plant in the indigenous soil wherever possible and save any necessary amendments as top dressing only. And certainly check with your county extension service first. They are the primary and best regional source for plant selection and care for home gardeners. That's what they were created for!!", "images": []}}

The cooktop is more or less centered on its wall, so it will look good.  Lining it up with the island is a non issue.  Everyone's brain likes symmetry, but when you have paid attention to the details on a hundred kitchens you will learn that a) there is way less symmetry in pretty kitchens than you imagine, and b) balance is far more important and better-feeling that a static, multi-way symmetrical space. other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "yuoutech-pfvwus-pf~1263861094", "author_name": "yuoutech", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/kitchen-and-bath-remodelers/yuoutech-pfvwus-pf~1263861094", "date": "2026-07-18", "text": "I would focus on finding a mirror and sconce finish with the same overall warmth as the Signature Hardware brushed gold, rather than expecting an exact one-brand match. Das Esszimmer ist aktuell einst\u00f6ckig. Der Esszimmerbereich (und Wintergarten) kann sicherlich f\u00fcr das 1. Vielleicht f\u00e4llt euch etwas ein, um sowohl vom Garten im Osten als auch der S\u00fcd-West Ausrichtung zu profitieren. 2. Im Eingangsbereich ausreichend Stauraum bzw. Garderobenbereich f\u00fcr mind. 4 Personen 3. Wir brauchen insgesamt Platz f\u00fcr 2 Kinderschlafzimmer, 1 Elternschlafzimmer, 1 Familienbad, 1 G\u00e4stezimmer und 1 B\u00fcrozimmer Vermutlich muss das EG komplett neu gestaltet werden. Auch im OG. ergeben sich durch die Erweiterung um die Fl\u00e4che des Esszimmers + \u201eWintergarten\u201c weitere Fl\u00e4chen f\u00fcr z.B. ein Familienbad + ggf. ein weiteres Kinderzimmer? Die K\u00fcchenform am liebsten mit (Halb-)Insel. Ich bin unsicher zwecks der  genauen Position. Ggf. l\u00e4sst sich nach Erweiterung im EG auch noch ein B\u00fcro oder G\u00e4stezimmer unterbringen? Wir brauchen au\u00dferdem viel mehr Platz f\u00fcr Garderobe usw im Eingangsbereich. Um Helligkeit in das ganze Haus zu bringen k\u00f6nnte man auch mit einer Glaswand/Stahl-Loftt\u00fcr arbeiten? Anbei die Zeichnungen auch mit Anzeige der Himmelsrichtungen. Wenn ihr ebenso Erfahrungen habt, was Einbau von Dachfenstern (im OG), Gauben (im Spitzboden) und Anbau (im Osten) 3-st\u00f6ckig, Erneuerung der Elektrik, neue B\u00e4der, in etwa kosten, w\u00e4re das abgesehen vom Grundriss auch total hilfreich. title: Kitchen extractor suitable for Asian/Malaysian cooking | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "zhanzhibar50", "author_name": "Suzana Campbell", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/zhanzhibar50", "date": "2026-03-14", "text": "Hello, I\u2019d really appreciate some advice please. We are currently renovating our kitchen into an open\u2011plan layout. As I\u2019m Malaysian, my cooking tends to involve a lot of frying and strongly aromatic dishes, so managing grease and smells is a big concern for me. We\u2019ve agreed on a 5\u2011hob cooktop positioned along the side wall (not on the island). I know this means I\u2019ll need a very effective extractor fan. My questions are: Any advice or real\u2011life experiences would be hugely appreciated. Thank you!", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "jonathandb1972", "author_name": "Jonathan", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/jonathandb1972", "date": "2026-03-14", "text": "Consider having more than one extractor.So perhaps one directly above the hob and one in the ceiling.To reduce noise you can also put a motor on the outside of the house.If you cook with oil consider getting a professional version of an extractor for grease filters. https://www.falmec.com/en-gb/products/gruppo-incasso-plus-pro/ You should also be researching plasma filters to reduce smells https://pando.es/en/eco-plasma/", "images": []}, "Comment 2": {"author_id": "zhanzhibar50", "author_name": "Suzana Campbell", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/zhanzhibar50", "date": "2026-03-16", "text": "Thank you forthe good advice Jonathan.  Following on from that, I did my research and have decided on  Falmec Cooker Hood Plane Plus NRS Wall 90 cm Black (quiet & strong suction)  &  Falmec Combined Filter Carbon-Zeo (for eliminating odour) but it seems nobody in UK sell these 2 items", "images": []}, "Comment 3": {"author_id": "jonathandb1972", "author_name": "Jonathan", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/jonathandb1972", "date": "2026-03-16", "text": "Whoever is supplying your kitchen should be able to source it", "images": []}, "Comment 4": {"author_id": "lifestyle-kitchens-pfvwgb-pf~1385883894", "author_name": "Lifestyle Kitchens", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/kitchen-designers-and-remodelers/lifestyle-kitchens-pfvwgb-pf~1385883894", "date": "2026-03-16", "text": "Assume that the extractor will be vented and not recirculating. For the power of the extractor [maximum output], this is measured in cubic meters per hour and this is the volume of air the extractor can move [subject to ducting restrictions like pipe size and bends]. For efficient extraction you need 10 air exchanges per hour so to work out the power of your extractor required for the space you have, work out the volume of the room [H x W x L] and multiply by 10 to give you the power required, https://www.tlc-direct.co.uk/Technical/DataSheets/Elica1/cooker-hood_calculator_1.htm Also the width of the extractor should be at least the width of the hob, but ideally up to about 1.5 times wider so you have a wider capture area for steam/smoke as it billows out when removing a pan lid. The type of hob, ie gas or induction, in theory also makes a difference to the width of the extractor required. Other tips like turning the extractor on when starting prep work so the room air is already flowing towards the extractor instead of when its already steaming/smoking also helps. title: Tiles or paint on bathroom walls | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "webuser-701893811", "author_name": "Niko G", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/webuser-701893811", "date": "2026-03-15", "text": "Redoing the bathroom and I wanted tiles all the way up. Contractor says that's unusual. Is it?", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "amystoller", "author_name": "amystoller", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/amystoller", "date": "2026-03-15", "text": "Do not accept your contractor's opinion on matters of taste. Do take your contractor's advice on board when it's a matter of code or another safety aspect, or what a decision may add to your cost, or helping to find a practical way to achieve something that may at first glance seem impossible. What size is the bathroom? What is/will be on the floor? What do/will the fixtures look like? What lighting will you have? What kind of tile do you want on your walls? What kind of soundproofing will the bathroom have? Tile all the way up on all the walls as well as on the floor is likely to create one heck of an echo chamber. Great if you plan to call your friends and family in to sing doo-wop, not so great if when you flush the toilet in the middle of the night it wakes up everyone in the house. Having tile will not keep the walls any cleaner than having paint. Both treatments have to be cleaned regularly. They don't stay clean on their own. Using paint designed for bathrooms and other humid areas is important. Other paints won't hold up as well. What will keep your walls dry on the inside is waterproofing. What will keep them dry on the visible surface is wiping down and dehumidifying the room. An exhaust fan can help with that.", "images": []}}

Then, since I was out there, moved my broccoli and cabbages outside the greenhouse as I am hardening them off to plant this week. Well, now I am covered in pollen and dog hair. title: U shaped kitchen worktop and sink materials and layout | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "stephen-hall11", "author_name": "Stephen Hall", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/stephen-hall11", "date": "2026-03-16", "text": "Hello, we inherited a 2019 laminate Howdens kitchen from a ground floor townhouse garage conversion which we like a lot but with some issues and I'd really appreciate some advice to help decide what we do next. It's a standard U shape with 4x600 cabinets. The maintenance issues are failing butt joints, particularly the one near the sink, and water collecting behind the sink and the worktop failing there - the tap has come loose several times and can't be tightened without special tool and blind access from below, and won't be able to tighten to the wood for much longer as it's now soft there. The other practical issue is the small bowl, which is our main place to wash everything but doesn't fit oven trays etc, which also creates more splash around the worktops! The plan was to address both by replacing the end worktop piece with a new sink - checking with Howdens it looks like we might get a match to the original design - but anyway we are struggling to decide what sink to go for (including tap location) and even if the worktop match is perfect we are being advised that we will have ongoing problems with the joint location by the sink and the second joint corner that's starting to lift further right. Replacing all worktops could easily lead into replacing the matching splashbacks! So before we start throwing money at this, we'd like to check whether this sort of wood finish is worth persevering with (compared to an alternative look) and in any case what sort of tap, sink and joint arrangement we should be looking for either now or in future.", "images": []}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "pfvwus-pf~1385883894", "author_name": "Lifestyle Kitchens", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/pfvwus-pf~1385883894", "date": "2026-03-20", "text": "Ideally any joints are 300mm away from sinks and hob cut outs but its not always possible. but tbh this looks like a poor worktop installation. The joint by the sink should of run the other way, looking at the lay out, i'd of probably had the window wall as full width. Looking at the pictures the sink has been poorly positioned and is to far back, the sink isn't suitable for a laminate worktop as the tap has to be fitted in the worktop [asking for trouble] instead of on the sink. For the tap if it isn't to far gone you need to get some silicon in the tap hole to seal the chipboard and refit the tap [you might need to remove the base unit back panel for decent access], also check if the sink and hob cutouts have been sealed. If the tap hole is to far gone then the worktop is ruined, i'd see if your house insurance covers this, but tbh its been poorly designed and badly fitted. The worktop joint should of been a masons mitre instead of a butt joint [looks like you can see the worktop edging in the joint]. I'd also advise having bullnose worktops instead of square edged [no chance of the edging failing with bullnose]. For a laminated worktop you need a top mounted sink with area for the tap to fit, you're not going to be able to just remove the sink run, all the worktop will need to come out, this will also affect the splashbacks/upstand as they'll be in the way. This is just 2 1/2 months new and if you zoom in the photo you can kind of see how the cast iron is getting oil stains that are subsequently baked on and can't easily be cleaned. This is just cleaned with the dirtier grates in the rear. The truth is this surface is an eyesore in an otherwise clean modern kitchen even when it's brand new. But it's a beast for serious cooking and function over form was the tradeoff I consciously made when deciding to buy it. The performance of these open burners is just phenomenal. What I'm looking for are real world suggestions from people that have lived with a bluestar or similar stove surface for a while. title: Water leaking into basement | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "dan-kane61", "author_name": "Dan Kane", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/dan-kane61", "date": "2026-03-18", "text": "Last summer we shortened our driveway so that it now stops at the front of our house and what used to be the driveway is now grass. It previously ran the full length of the house. After doing this, we started getting water in the basement whenever there was medium to heavy rain (anything more than a quarter of an inch in an hour). The area where we get the leak is right by the basement door, and while we previously thought this was water coming under the door we now believe it's due to water coming in thru a leaky foundation wall. Attaching a picture of where we're seeing water pooling.I understand that excavating and waterproofing the exterior is the best solution, though I'm wondering if there are other solutions like installing a French drain in the new yard that might be equally effective if they're able to move the water before it gets to the house. The yard itself is graded and the gutters all feed out the street so those aren't options. Also, for reference, the door is about seven feet below ground level", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/b7f1a25509ba9ec9_8031-w500-h666-b0-p0--.jpg"]}
other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "gn-builders-l-l-c-pfvwus-pf~1476403835", "author_name": "GN Builders L.L.C", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/general-contractors/gn-builders-l-l-c-pfvwus-pf~1476403835", "date": "2026-04-14", "text": "Could be many reasons, just a few to list: water gets trapped between the driveway and the house in a grass area, not enough pitch from the house to the driveway, or gutters discharge into the grass area, and without proper drainage, an excessive amount of water percolates near the foundation and finds its way into the basement. Posting a few pictures of the outside will be more helpful.", "images": []}, "Comment 2": {"author_id": "lf-builders-pfvwus-pf~794048028", "author_name": "LF Builders", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/general-contractors/lf-builders-pfvwus-pf~794048028", "date": "2026-05-19", "text": "The old driveway was doing water management work even if that wasn't the goal. Impervious surface against the house sheds rainfall toward the street. Grass soaks it in. Pull enough of that surface and the same volume that previously ran off is now infiltrating within a few feet of the foundation wall. The French drain is worth pricing out. It intercepts surface water before it gets to the footing, which works when the wall itself is still sound and the problem is water reaching it from above. Less invasive and cheaper than excavation by a fair margin. It won't be enough if the foundation wall has a failed dampproofing layer, cracked parging, or a gap at the footing-wall joint. A French drain controls what happens in the surrounding soil, not what happens at the wall face. When the wall is the problem, exterior waterproofing (excavation to footing depth, membrane, drainage board) is the actual fix. Does the leak show up during rain, or a day or two after? Rain-concurrent leaks tend to be surface infiltration, which makes the French drain route more viable. Delayed leaks, or leaks after snowmelt with no active rain, point to hydrostatic pressure against a wall that's no longer sealed. At seven feet below grade with a wall-entry point, I'd want to see the wall condition before recommending either. A contractor-side breakdown of how this scopes out, interior vs. exterior, and what pushes the decision one way: https://home.renovation.reviews/t/basement-waterproofing-in-ontario-interior-vs-exterior-and-what-a-good-quote-actually-covers-2026/47643", "images": []}, "Comment 3": {"author_id": "ursa-pro-pfvwus-pf~441722354", "author_name": "Ursa-pro", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/professionals/plumbers/ursa-pro-pfvwus-pf~441722354", "date": "2026-08-07", "text": "The timing is a pretty strong clue. If the basement only started leaking after the driveway was shortened, changing that surface may have changed where a significant amount of rainwater is going. Personally, I'd diagnose the water path first, then decide between improving exterior drainage and waterproofing the foundation. Otherwise there's a risk of paying for a French drain and discovering that the wall itself was the problem.", "images": []}}

title: Report on my second winter in Zone 5 | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "rosefollyz5", "author_name": "Rosefolly z5", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/rosefollyz5", "date": "2026-03-20", "text": "Perhaps this is a bit early to report since I understand that we often get snow here in April or even May.  But so far this has shaped up to be a winter that would be considered mild even in zone 6.  We have had below freezing days (a few) and snow on the ground (a little).  Still, even last winter, our first here, considered mild by long time locals, had considerably more bite than this one did.  Since our temperatures are expected to be in the 60's-80's for the foreseeable future, I'm going to consider winter to be over for all practical purposes.  I have removed my wire rose mulch cages so the new young shoots could get some light, though I have not yet removed the mulch that did not fall away by itself. I had some failures last year with roses rated for zone 5.  I did not replant any of them. All but one of my Buck roses died down to the ground so I removed them.  The hardy exception was April Moon, a pale yellow that fades nicely to white so it looks perfect in my nearly-white garden.  Moonlight Romantica died, too.  It was probably too strong a yellow for this garden, so I decided not to mourn it. The rose that suffered most from the cold this year was Buff Beauty, with all the canes that were not covered in mulch dying to the line of protection.  I have a particular affecton for Buff Beauty, so as long as it survives, it has a place here. With that amount of dieback I doubt it will ever get to the size of my gorgeous California speciman from which it is a rooted cutting.  For this reason I will probably not try any more Hybrid Musks. My two Canadian shrub roses had no cane dieback.  They are Morden Snowbeauty and Oscar Peterson. My two albas Armide and Jeanne d'Arc had only a shovel of mulch at the base, and zero cane dieback.  That is why I am so eager to add another white alba. My damasks Botzaris and Madame Hardy are small enough that they were mostly covered by mulch, but also had no cane dieback.  I expect them to take off this year.  In the front, away from the white garden, I am growing two gallicas Tuscany Superb and Rosa Mundi.  Like my other once blooming European OGRs, they suffered no dieback, but unlike them, they seem to be off to a very slow start. I have always loved these historic roses and am pleased to be in a climate where they should thrive.  Also since they are once bloomers, the Japanese beetles don't pay a lot of attention to them, certainly a bonus. I do have an Austin rose planted, Winchester Cathedral.  No cane dieback in this mild winter year.  I have another Austin on order, Susan Williams-Ellis. Now for the oher modern repeat blooming roses considered hardy.  I grow Icecap and Snowdrift.  Both lost no canes, hurray.  (Not fragrant though, alas.) Marie Pavie also seems very hardy and it is fragrant. I have also planted Bolero, Champagne Wishes, Cloud 10 (climber), White Eden (another climber), and Top Cream.  Still smallish, but this year at least, they seem less hardy to cold than the European OGRs but hardier than the hybrid musk or the rest of the Buck roses I tried last year. BTW, in addition to the Austin Susan Williams-Ellis, I also have the rambler Alberic Barbier on order. I had considered Ghislaine de Feligonde but I need more input as to its tolerance to my climate.", "images": []}

title: Organic Cotton vs. Recycled Polyester Athletic Wear: Which Is Actually | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "hu-238414988-pfvwes-pf~1767140487", "author_name": "HU-238414988", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/not-specified/hu-238414988-pfvwes-pf~1767140487", "date": "2026-03-24", "text": "You're paying attention to what you buy. You see \"made from recycled bottles\" and you assume you're making the right choice. The activewear industry has done exceptional marketing work to make recycled polyester feel like the sustainable default. It isn't. And the full comparison between organic cotton and recycled polyester athletic wear almost never gets done transparently. What Most Sustainable Activewear Marketing Gets Wrong Recycled polyester (rPET) has a genuine benefit: it diverts plastic bottles from landfill and reduces demand for virgin petroleum. That's real. But the conversation about rPET typically stops there, before reaching the downstream problems that make it a questionable choice for athletic wear specifically. Every time you wash a synthetic workout shirt, it sheds microplastic fibers. Studies estimate 700,000 or more microplastic particles per wash cycle for synthetic garments. Wastewater treatment captures less than 70% of these. The rest enters waterways, accumulates in marine ecosystems, and ends up in fish tissue -- and eventually in the food chain. The \"sustainable\" garment made from recycled bottles is still plastic touching your skin. It still sheds plastic into waterways. It still doesn't biodegrade. It's a better outcome than virgin polyester, but it's not a clean outcome. Organic athletic wear made from certified organic cotton tells a different lifecycle story entirely. Recycled polyester solves one environmental problem while creating others. Organic cotton addresses the full lifecycle from farm to disposal. How to Actually Evaluate Athletic Wear Sustainability Fiber Biodegradability Organic cotton is a natural cellulose fiber. At end of life, it decomposes. Recycled polyester is still plastic. It doesn't biodegrade -- it fragments into smaller and smaller plastic particles indefinitely. For any garment you plan to eventually discard, this is the most fundamental lifecycle difference. Microplastic Shedding in Wash Organic cotton workout shirts shed natural fibers in the wash. Those fibers are cellulose -- they break down in aquatic environments. Synthetic fibers, including rPET, shed plastic microfibers that accumulate. If you wash athletic wear weekly, that's 50+ microplastic-shedding cycles per year, per garment. Chemical Safety on Skin GOTS certification -- the standard for certified organic textiles -- prohibits a specific list of hazardous substances in processing. Azo dyes, heavy metals, formaldehyde, phthalates. Recycled polyester has no equivalent standard. The \"recycled\" label says nothing about what chemical processing was used to create the fiber or what residues remain in the finished garment. Agricultural vs. Petroleum Sourcing Organic cotton comes from a renewable, biological source. Even accounting for the land and water used to grow cotton, certified organic farming avoids the synthetic pesticide and fertilizer inputs that create the most significant agricultural externalities. Recycled polyester is still derived from petroleum -- a non-renewable resource. Carbon Footprint Comparison This one is genuinely more complex. rPET production has a lower carbon footprint than virgin polyester. Organic cotton farming typically has a higher carbon footprint per unit than conventional cotton but a better land and water quality profile. The honest answer is that neither fiber is clearly superior on all climate metrics -- but organic cotton wins decisively on end-of-life, microplastics, and chemical safety. Practical Criteria for Making the Switch Ask what certification backs the claim. \"Recycled\" is verifiable; \"eco-friendly\" is not. For organic cotton, GOTS is the relevant standard. Verify it on the public database before buying. Prioritize the garments with most skin contact first. Workout shirts and underwear have the highest sustained skin contact during exercise. If you're making one swap, make it there before worrying about outerwear. Evaluate the washing behavior. Organic cotton workout shirts can be washed at moderate temperatures without fiber degradation or significant microplastic contribution. rPET improves with a microplastic-catching laundry bag -- but that's an added step addressing a problem that organic cotton doesn't create. Think about full lifecycle, not just manufacturing. The garment you're buying will eventually be retired. Where it goes when you're done with it matters. Natural fibers compost. Plastic fibers don't. Recognize that rPET and organic cotton aren't equivalent choices. Both are better than virgin polyester conventional cotton. But they're not equivalent. The person who's thought carefully about both and chosen organic cotton has made a more complete sustainability decision. Why the Organic vs. Recycled Question Matters Now The activewear market is growing faster than its sustainability standards. Brands have strong incentive to use \"recycled\" and \"eco\" language that resonates with health-conscious consumers without requiring full lifecycle accountability. If the market defaults to rPET as the sustainable standard, we get a generation of activewear that solves plastic bottle waste while accelerating microplastic ocean contamination. That's a trade-off that rarely gets disclosed in marketing. Organic athletic wear -- specifically, GOTS-certified organic cotton -- represents a genuinely different model. It starts with regenerative-adjacent farming practices that prohibit the most harmful pesticides. It processes without the prohibited chemical classes. It biodegrades at end of life without microplastic contribution. The environmental premium you pay for organic athletic wear isn't just about feeling good. It's about the full lifecycle of the thing you're buying. And on that full lifecycle comparison, organic cotton wins more dimensions than the recycled polyester narrative would have you believe.", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/2722783909c29bf6_1591-w500-h282-b0-p0--.jpg"]}

title: The Best Underwear for Men Who Sit All Day (Office Workers, Remote Pro | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "hu-56074441-pfvwau-pf~1708420301", "author_name": "HU-56074441", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/not-specified/hu-56074441-pfvwau-pf~1708420301", "date": "2026-03-24", "text": "Eight hours in a chair means eight hours of compressed, occluded, synthetic fabric pressed against your most temperature-sensitive anatomy. Most men have filed this discomfort under \"just how things are.\" It doesn't have to be. The underwear designed for athletes performing explosive movements is not the same underwear that serves a desk worker best. Here's what the physiological reality of prolonged sitting actually demands. What Sitting All Day Does to Underwear Performance When you sit, the contact surface between your underwear and your body changes dramatically compared to standing or moving. Compressed against a chair, synthetic fabric does two things poorly: it traps heat by preventing air circulation from below, and it creates sustained pressure at the waistband and leg opening contact points that becomes progressively more irritating over an eight-hour session. The scrotal temperature increase from prolonged sitting is documented in research on male fertility and occupational health. A seated posture reduces air circulation around the scrotal area. Synthetic fabric amplifies this by acting as an insulating layer. By the end of an eight-hour workday, the temperature differential between ideal scrotal temperature and actual scrotal temperature in synthetic underwear while seated can be significant. For men working remotely \u2014 where there's no social consequence to \"airing out\" and every incentive to prioritize comfort \u2014 the difference between synthetic and natural fiber underwear for seated work is immediately apparent. Eight hours of seated pressure in synthetic underwear creates a cumulative discomfort that you've normalized as the price of desk work. It's not. It's the price of the wrong fabric. What to Look For in Organic Cotton Boxer Briefs for Desk Work Temperature Management in Compressed Position Organic cotton breathes passively. Even in compressed contact with a chair, the fiber structure allows some heat and moisture exchange. Synthetic fabrics create a sealed thermal environment under compression \u2014 no air exchange, no heat dissipation, just progressive accumulation. For eight hours of seated work, this difference is not marginal. Soft Waistband Construction for Extended Wear An athletic waistband engineered for high-output physical activity creates sustained pressure at a specific line around your waist during seated work. It's fine for an hour of training. It's irritating after hour six at a desk. Organic cotton boxer briefs with a wide, soft waistband and cotton inlay under the elastic distribute pressure more evenly and eliminate the friction line that develops during long seated days. Non-Restrictive Leg Opening Seated posture brings the leg opening of boxer briefs into sustained contact with the inner thigh. A tight leg opening under office clothing becomes a compression source at the femoral blood vessels. A properly sized leg opening in organic cotton maintains fit without creating sustained restriction during the seated hours when this contact is constant. Moisture Management Without Synthetic Saturation Desk workers don't sweat heavily, but they do produce background moisture throughout the day. Organic cotton absorbs this moisture into its fiber structure and manages it gradually. Synthetic fabric that \"wicks\" moisture to its outer surface creates a damp outer layer in contact with pants \u2014 which is both uncomfortable and visible in certain office situations. Odor Performance Over a Full Work Day Without the airflow of physical activity, odor compounds accumulate more in sedentary wear than during exercise. Cotton's fiber structure is less hospitable to odor-causing bacteria than synthetic fiber surfaces, making end-of-workday freshness meaningfully better in natural fiber underwear. Practical Advice for Office and Remote Workers Stand and walk at least once per hour. This is good for your health generally and also briefly interrupts the thermal accumulation of prolonged sitting. Even a 2-minute standing break changes the compression and ventilation state of your underwear environment. Match your underwear fabric to your climate control environment. Air-conditioned offices can be cold. If you run cold, slightly heavier organic cotton is more appropriate than the lightest-weight athletic option. Remote workers in non-climate-controlled home offices have different needs in summer versus winter. Consider boxer brief cut versus brief cut for seated work. Boxer briefs maintain consistent contact with the inner thigh throughout sitting and standing transitions without riding up or bunching. Briefs are more compact but can create more intense concentrated pressure during prolonged sitting. Avoid waistband compression under fitted clothing. If you're wearing slim trousers over your underwear, a wide waistband adds bulk at the waist that may be visible or uncomfortable under tailored office wear. Choose a waistband profile appropriate to your outer clothing style. Why Desk Work Is the Highest-Stakes Use Case Exercise-related underwear performance is measured in hours. Desk-work underwear performance is measured over an 8-to-10-hour window that repeats five days a week for 50 weeks a year. The accumulation is substantial. Most men buy underwear with athletic activity in mind and wear it for desk work 90% of the time. The sustained thermal and mechanical demands of prolonged sitting are different from those of a gym session \u2014 and the fabric that solves one doesn't automatically solve the other. Organic cotton boxer briefs with soft, non-compressive construction address the desk worker's specific demands better than athletic-optimized synthetic gear. For the man whose workday is largely sedentary, this is the more relevant performance context.", "images": ["https://st.hzcdn.com/fimgs/cc72150209c2c0fc_1068-w500-h282-b0-p0--.jpg"]}

title: Anyone familiar with hoarding? | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "sephia-wa", "author_name": "sephia_wa", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/sephia-wa", "date": "2026-03-24", "text": "Anyone have any experience with hoarding? It is a horrible thing. I lost a cousin back in November who was a hoarder. I knew she was and hadn't been to her home in recent years. She was 74 and had a couple of health issues. I hadn't been able to reach her and was getting ready to contact the sheriff to do a welfare check when a friend of hers messaged me via Facebook. The pastor of their church had the sheriff do the welfare check, and sadly my cousin was found deceased - lying on a heap of junk and garbage. I asked the coroner if she sees this often, hoarding situations. She said yes, it is more common than you would think. And this is in a small, island community. I asked the coroner if she knew the cause of hoarding, why what we would normally think of \"clutter\" can get so out of control. She said from what she knew, the cause is still a bit unknown. I did some research, and according to the American Psychiatric Association, the definitive cause is unknown but is believed to be related to anxiety/OCD. I know my cousin had a bit of a strange childhood - her mom, my aunt, was a bit weird. Extreme religiosity, kept the drapes closed to ward off \"spirits,\" etc. I don't know if that upbringing manifested as hoarding with my cousin. Those hoarding shows? My cousins home looked like that. Anyone familiar with hoarding? It is such a strange thing, how people can live amongst garbage, junk, and filth, and on the outside appear normal. My cousin did research at the University of Washington, was really smart, and outwardly appeared like anyone else.", "images": []}

In a collection, the goal is achieving a positive emotion, whereas hoarding is avoiding a negative emotion.   I used to think hoarding was an addiction, but addictions are about achieving a positive emotional response (from the substance or the activity), but hoarding is about avoiding a negative emotional response. main_question: {"author_id": "melissaaipapa", "author_name": "Melissa Northern Italy zone 8", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/melissaaipapa", "date": "2026-03-25", "text": "This morning my helper and I stopped on the way back from town to pick up more of the wood shavings by the side of the road, left over from wood-cutting operations.  I don't know how cost-effective this is, since I'm paying my helper to assist me in gathering it, but re-use has a value of its own.  We filled one large black garbage bag, normally used for our paper recycling, and twenty twenty-liter bags that had previously held compost bought from the store.  I now have a lifetime supply of these last, but they're great for trash and recycling.  This was as much wood shavings as we could fit in the Panda, and we had to tie down the rear hatch. The weather is fair and warm for the season, but the wind is picking up today, forecast to bring a drop in temperatures, which is fine with me.  It's still March, not yet time for balmy airs.  We could use rain to water the garden, but there's none in the forecast.  Ground water supplies are good. The roses are leafing out marvelously now, buds forming on the Teas.  The wisteria is also forming buds; the forsythia is a blaze of yellow.  Sweet violets are fading, while the Viola sororia in the alley, scentless but otherwise lovely, is in bloom.  This one is the form V.sororia priceana; I want the white form, but have to find someplace dire enough to contain its exuberance.  The alley is perfect but taken. Yesterday I set my helper to cleaning out the shade garden.  There are pretty things going on there, but I can't appreciate them while it's such a mess.  I pulled nettles for a couple of hours until I got tired.  It looked better afterwards, though my helper does have a tendency to make tabula rasa which I'm trying to discourage.  He sure got the nettles and lemon balm out, though.  The Paeonia 'mollis' was largely spared after I showed it, though I'm not sure some two-leaved babies weren't wiped out....I had told him not to work there.  It seeds very nicely in its miserable spot, and makes a show for a few days every spring.  Today my helper is pulling dead grass in the roses and shrubs, weeding nettles he didn't already get yesterday, and making the shade garden, not only prettier, but more approachable for me, so I can look over the roses and do a bit of pruning.  I sure am looking forward to getting the motor scythe back:  that should take care of the rest of the tidying. So, that's it for today. main_question: {"author_id": "nanabeth", "author_name": "lizbeth-gardener", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/nanabeth", "date": "2026-03-25", "text": "I like a slice of toast with breakfast and an occasional sandwich, but don't go thru a loaf quick enough to keep from spoiling and can only use so many bread crumbs and bread pudding. other_comments: {"Comment 1": {"author_id": "plllog", "author_name": "plllog", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/plllog", "date": "2026-03-25", "text": "Agreed that trying it is the only way you'll know, but the problem is likely the evaporator if you have a newfangled freezer.  It dries things out (I know--duh).  If you're quick freezing the bread first, I don't see that you'll have a big difference between the container and a quality freezer rated zip bag, but maybe the vacuum really will help.  I freeze some slices at a time, but usually at least four, in the wrapper if bought, to best identify it, and a zip bag, and other than a bit of drying out, which is normal for frozen cut bread, it comes out just fine. The big issue is likely in the freezing process.  That's when the most loose water crystalizes and becomes icy, though following that, there's water migration, which happens continuously, though slowly, with any frozen bread, even in a total manual defrost freezer. title: On the density of woods... | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "upperbaygardener", "author_name": "UpperBayGardener (zone 7)", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/user/upperbaygardener", "date": "2026-03-26", "text": "I've done more chainsawin' this winter and spring than ever before...at least on my own ornamentals vs. junk I inherited with the property like red maples.  This means I have to schlep around with yard with the trimmings. I think it's striking how the density of wood varies.  Here's my very informal ranking...from lightest to heaviest. Taxodium hybrids T406 and T502.  Holy mackerel, these are like balsa wood.  But surprisingly strong!  You have be very careful to undercut when removing a branch, the wood is super stringy and will shred easily...it will start tearing and striping into the bark layer of the trunk. Larch - very light as well, it's a close call between these, but I think the taxodium has the edge. Japanese fir - the next lightest conifer.  Although the foliage isn't scented like other firs, the branches are quite resinous when you cut them.  And the sap does have a bit of a smell. ----- Magnolias - the lightest hardwood probably goes here. Thuja 'Green Giant'.  Tree had been dead for a year, so this might be heavier with water it in. Norway spruce - somewhere in here.  The ones compared in this section (2 up, 2 down) are all pretty close. Celtis - had a small weed tree I removed.  Better to get them when they're small! Ulmus parviflora ----- Red maples are around here, definitely heavier than the previous ones Pinus taeda or (1/2 P. \u00d7 sondereggeri) - now we get to the heavy softwoods.  I was shocked when I trimmed the first large branch of this and tried to move it.   I had to make another cut. Yew - SUPER heavy.  It's hard to compare exactly though, because the thickest branch was only about 2/3 as thick as the Pine. Quercus bicolor Quercus variabilis - Lawd have mercy these are heavy!  Like picking up steel pipe!", "images": []}

title: Negative Keywords on Amazon: The Most Overlooked Tactic Your Agency Sh | Houzz Forum
main_question: {"author_id": "hu-87167812-pfvwes-pf~1137987666", "author_name": "HU-87167812", "author_url": "https://www.houzz.com/hznb/professionals/not-specified/hu-87167812-pfvwes-pf~1137987666", "date": "2026-03-28", "text": "Your auto campaign has been running for four months. You pulled the search term report last week and found that $800 in ad spend went to \"yoga mat bag\" clicks on your sports water bottle listing. Zero conversions. You're selling water bottles. Buyers looking for yoga mat bags have no interest in your product. That $800 is gone. And without a systematic negative keyword process, next month will look similar. Negative keyword management is unglamorous work. It doesn't appear in case studies or agency pitch decks. But it's one of the most reliable ways to improve ACoS \u2014 and most Amazon sellers aren't doing it systematically. Why Negative Keywords Matter More Than Most Sellers Realize? Amazon's auto campaigns match your product to search queries based on listing content. The algorithm is broad and opportunistic. It will match your listing to adjacent and sometimes completely irrelevant queries if it detects any keyword overlap. Those matches generate impressions, sometimes clicks, and almost never purchases. Every click from an irrelevant search query is wasted spend. Over weeks and months, these waste clicks add up to a meaningful percentage of total ad spend producing zero revenue. The cumulative ACoS impact of eliminating irrelevant clicks compounds over time. The search term report is your evidence base. It shows you every search query that triggered one of your ads, how many clicks it generated, and what it converted. Queries with multiple clicks and zero conversions are either irrelevant or reveal a listing problem. Either way, they're costing money they shouldn't. An amazon ads agency handling your account should review search term reports and add negative keywords systematically \u2014 not just when performance problems are obvious. Negative keyword management is like expense management. No individual waste item seems important enough to prioritize. But the cumulative savings across all waste items are significant and compound indefinitely once captured. Building a Negative Keyword Discovery Workflow Weekly Search Term Report Review Pull your search term report weekly for all active campaigns \u2014 not monthly. High-spend, low-converting queries that run for four weeks without a negative added represent significant accumulated waste. A weekly review cycle catches them early. Sort the report by spend descending. The most expensive non-converting queries are your priority targets. A query that's generated $50 in spend and zero conversions is more important to negative than one that's generated $5. Conversion-Based Threshold Criteria Set explicit criteria for when a search term becomes a negative candidate. A common framework: Explicit criteria prevent inconsistent application and ensure the workflow runs mechanically rather than relying on subjective review. Campaign-Level vs. Ad Group-Level Placement Negative keywords can be added at the campaign level (blocking across all ad groups in a campaign) or the ad group level (blocking only within a specific ad group). Campaign-level negatives are appropriate for broad irrelevance \u2014 a query that's irrelevant to your entire campaign. Ad group-level negatives are appropriate when a query might be relevant in one ad group but not another. Match Type Considerations Negative exact match blocks only that precise query. Negative phrase match blocks any query containing that phrase. Choose match type based on how broadly you need to block: Be cautious with broad negative phrase blocking \u2014 it can inadvertently block relevant queries that contain similar words. Proactive Negative List Building Beyond reactive search term report review, agencies should build proactive negative lists from the start of a campaign. Before launching, identify the most obvious irrelevant query categories for your product type. A children's toy brand should immediately add adult category negatives. A premium product should add \"cheap\" and \"budget\" as negatives from day one. A brand-specific product should negative competitor brand names to prevent wasted spend from searchers who aren't considering switching. These proactive negatives save the spend that would otherwise go to learning that these queries don't convert \u2014 spend that never needed to happen. Frequently Asked Questions What is negative keyword management and why is it critical for Amazon PPC? Negative keyword management involves identifying and blocking irrelevant search queries that trigger your ads but don't convert. Every click from an irrelevant query wastes ad spend, and these waste clicks compound over months\u2014making systematic negative keyword management one of the most reliable ways to improve ACoS, even though it's often overlooked. How often should you review search term reports for negative keywords? You should pull and review search term reports weekly for all active campaigns, not monthly. Weekly reviews catch high-spend, low-converting queries early before they accumulate significant wasted budget over four weeks or longer. What threshold criteria should you use to identify negative keyword candidates? A common framework is three or more clicks with zero conversions as a trigger to review query relevance. You should prioritize by spend descending, focusing first on the most expensive non-converting queries\u2014for example, a query that generated $50 in spend with zero conversions is a higher priority negative than one that cost $5. How does Amazon's auto campaign algorithm contribute to irrelevant clicks? Amazon's auto campaigns match products to search queries based on listing content using a broad algorithm that detects keyword overlap. The system is opportunistic and will match your listing to adjacent and sometimes completely irrelevant queries if it finds any content similarity, generating impressions and clicks from buyers searching for entirely different products. Why should you work with an Amazon ads agency for negative keyword management? An experienced Amazon PPC agency handles weekly search term report reviews systematically across all campaigns, catching wasteful queries before they accumulate significant spend. This ongoing, disciplined approach to negative keyword discovery is rare among individual sellers and represents a meaningful competitive advantage in cost management. Tracking the Impact of Negative Keyword Management Measure your waste percentage \u2014 spend on zero-conversion queries as a percentage of total spend \u2014 monthly. A well-managed account should have a declining waste percentage over time as the negative keyword library grows. A flat or rising waste percentage indicates the workflow isn't running consistently. The cumulative savings from systematic negative keyword management over a twelve-month engagement are significant. The agencies that track and demonstrate this impact on a monthly basis are the ones treating negative keyword management as a strategic function rather than housekeeping. Make sure yours does.", "images": []}

We are finding the roof tile choice tricky. The house (late 1940s) will be give a relative modern look and will have a white render.  We will have intergrated solar panels that will feature on the roof at the front of the house (for best sun position). At the solar will feature so prominantly we are keen for it to be as seamless as possible and not stand out. The quote we have had for slate (Glendyne) for supply and fit is fair but way over our budget. We had looked at Marley Edgemere concrete tiles in Anthracite - however I'm concerned as on the colour fade with concrete tiles over the years and how that will look with solar panels which would  stand out more. Considering now Cedreal (fibre cerment tiles) in Cedral Riverdale in Blue/Black or Graphite. Anyone have any experience with best roof tiles when using intergrated solar panels at front of the house - where slate appears to be too expensive? And best colour choice so they don't stand out - blue/black or graphite? Thanks in advance for any views!", "images": []}

My style leans traditional/transitional with a calming, serene feel and a subtle nod to coastal\u2014muted blues, greens, and soft taupes. That said, I\u2019m finding it incredibly challenging to make everything feel cohesive, especially without being able to see materials and colors in the actual space. I\u2019ve noticed myself defaulting to white for everything\u2026 and my husband is starting to push back a bit \ud83d\ude0a At this point, our kitchen design is finalized, along with the fireplace surround using Jerica Ceniza porcelain tile laid in a brick pattern (https://www.tileshop.com/products/jerica-ceniza-porcelain-wall-and-floor-tile-3-x-12-in-681720). We\u2019ve selected Coretec Cairo Oak LVP (https://coretecfloors.com/en-us/products/coretec-pro-enhanced/cairo-oak-vv491-02956) for flooring throughout, and the stairs will coordinate with the same flooring, accented by black wrought iron. I also have two of the kids\u2019 bedrooms planned, but beyond that, I feel completely stuck. We\u2019re in the final month before moving back home, and the decision fatigue is very real. I\u2019m especially struggling with selecting cabinet paint colors and making sure everything flows seamlessly from one space to the next. The past eight months have been incredibly difficult for our family, and more than anything, I want our home to feel calm, peaceful, and safe again for our kids. One of the biggest challenges is our open living room/kitchen layout\u2014specifically the corner fireplace. With 8-foot ceilings, I\u2019m unsure whether to carry the fireplace tile all the way to the ceiling or stop at the mantel. Most of the full-height fireplace designs I\u2019m drawn to are in homes with taller ceilings, and I worry that approach may make our space feel smaller. I\u2019m also torn between a simple solid wood mantel and a more detailed craftsman-style surround, and I\u2019m unsure how to design the adjacent wall so it feels intentional and cohesive. Another space I\u2019m struggling with is the bathroom shared by our two young boys and guests. I love the look of black-and-white checkerboard porcelain tile laid in a diamond pattern, but I worry it may feel too busy in a smaller space or limit flexibility over time. The alternative would be continuing the Coretec Cairo Oak LVP into the bathroom for a more seamless look, but I\u2019m concerned that might feel too plain or lack character. The final space I\u2019m really struggling with is the primary bathroom. We\u2019ll have a freestanding tub, Kingston brushed brass fixtures, and a white 3x12 subway tile with subtle movement for the shower. I\u2019m stuck on selecting the flooring and vanity color (the vanity will be custom painted, as wood tones aren\u2019t an option right now). I absolutely love marble, but with kids and everyday wear, porcelain feels like the more practical choice.
